I'm not sure if this is the right place to post this ( @HomerSimpson if I'm in the wrong place just let me know and I'll delete it) but I wanted to say thank you to FPH.

I've always been a heavier girl, 20 to 40 pounds over weight. I never felt comfortable with my body, I never showed it off despite being blessed with genetics that made most of the weight go to tits and ass. (Think original definition of curvy before the planets ruined it.) I never actually admitted to myself that I was gross but deep down I felt disgusting. That no guy would ever date or love me because I was heavier. It was hard on my self-esteem because I was surrounded by thinner women, more normal women. Even my mum is smaller (is classified overweight with BMI but the woman wrestles with horses and sheep everyday. She's pretty much built like a brick shit house so she gets a pass in my eyes. She's got no jiggle, even after having five kids.) I was surrounded by people lighter than me, one of the joys of living in a farming community where people moved more than they ate.

I was unhappy and then when I was on Reddit and the Fattening happened I became aware of FPH and I was horrified. Well, at first. I hated that it was a space dedicated to hating a certain type of people. Being bullied (not for my weight mind you) it made me empathetic to these poor creatures but then I moved to Voat. I kept away because I HATED that you made me feel shame about how I was because I was shaming myself enough already. Then I started visiting more and more and then something happened.

My mum and I love to collect rocks. Its kind of like a bonding thing. We go for walks and collect rocks and this particular day we found a very good spot and picked quite a few rocks. I was wearing a very large button up shirt over a tank top and so I was carrying the rocks in my shirt. It started to get heavier and heavier the more rocks we found. By the time we were ready to go home my knees and hips hurt. I could barely bed down without hurting and getting up was terrible. I laughed about it, asking if that is what it felt like to be pregnant. We walked home and it turns out I was carrying 30 pounds of rocks in my shirt. Just an extra 30 pounds wreaked havoc on my joints and back. It fucked with my mobility and my ability to do simple things. The walk home left me winded and sore and suddenly understood what you guys have been talking about.

I did not want to become that which I had sympathized with. I didn't want to become an Obeast. It terrified me to the point where I started counting my calories the very next day. I was 5'3" and 165 pounds. A BMI over 29. You beautiful shitlords made me scared enough that in the past eight weeks I have dropped 16 pounds. I know it doesn't seem like much but I stepped on the scale and cried when I saw that I was 149. It was the first time I had been under 150 since I was 14 and I bawled like a baby because I was so happy I had succeeded in doing that.

So thank you guys. Thank you for showing me just what it meant to be overweight. Thank you for giving me the motivation to better myself. Thank you for giving me the drive to lose enough weight that I have to buy new pants because I can fit my legs and my arms into my old ones at the same time. Thank you for kicking me in ass enough for me to now have troubles grabbing onto my tummy fat because it's slowly disappearing. Thank you for showing me that these disgusting butterballs do not deserve my sympathy because they brought it onto themselves. And thank you for shaming me enough to get my ass in gear to make myself happier because fatter was not better. Not for me.

I still have a ways to go. My BMI is now 26, not low enough to be a shitlady but I hope to get there soon. So until then I hope you guys don't mind me being one of the lurking fatties on FPH. (I do mind the rules though. I don't upvoat or participate at all. I want to work my way to that and for me it seems like that would be a victory that would be so much sweeter.) But at least know that this fatty is a work in progress and it's all thanks to your beautiful shitlording.

King Muhammad bin Nayef sits alone in his quarters, staring at a stack of papers, not even really reading the words. Someone knocks on the door and the king mumbles something along the lines of 'come in.'

A stately woman enters the room. Since the CPVPV had stopped patrolling the streets enforcing Sharia, women became more able to travel freely. The king didn't mind, it made the logistics of day to day activities much less complicated. "My king, I heard of your press release on the KBS."

King Muhammad lifts his head from the reports in front of him and nods. "Yes, the international community was quite upset. I really had no choice. I doubt we would've avoided armed conflict should I have gone through with the project."

"But king, wasn't that the point?"

King Muhammad sighs "No, not really. I wanted other countries to begin deploying defensive measures into space. I wanted militaries to take their first step into Allah's heavens. If I could've gotten world militaries into space, the world would have been made much more interested in the advancement of space travel technology. Reusable rockets might have been developed in less than a decade. I might have lived to see the first ship sent to Alpha Centauri."

"But now-"

"But now, while everyone seems more interested in space, science is the only thing pushing us forward. With the amendment to the Outer Space Treaty, space is not even an option for world militaries. And purely science has never been a good enough motivator for progress. Without a good nudge like the one I had in store, we'll be grounded for a while."

The woman looks down at her feet, her face lost in thought.

"Tell the other engineers that I think you all did a good job."

The woman looks up "But we didn't even get a chance to finish the satellite."

"But it would've worked. We both know that"

"Thanks, King."
